A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same score-matching theory and Bootstrapped Score Matching method. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and revised material.

before.justification: v1 Figure 1 and Appendix F.1 report original DSM-versus-BSM experiments on Gaussian score estimation and sampling from a one-dimensional Gaussian mixture.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments in Figure 3 and Appendix G.1 and adds an original Gaussian dimension-scaling experiment in Figure 1 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The joint DSM objective, sequential BSM procedure, bootstrapped targets, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The new dimension-scaling experiment applies existing DSM; it does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled Gaussian scenario spanning ten data dimensions from 10 to 200, with covariance eigenvalues sampled in [1, 2]. This modestly expands the synthetic input conditions tested while retaining the original Gaussian and one-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments.

E2.justification: DSM remains the evaluated comparator to BSM in both original experiments. The linear-dimension reference curve in v2 Figure 1 is a theoretical scaling comparison, not an additional implemented competing method.

E3.justification: The added dimension-scaling study introduces 1,000 training and 1,000 held-out samples, a two-layer network with hidden size 1,000, 200 epochs, and 100 timesteps. Its evaluation averages score error across time and normalizes by parameter count and log log d. These are settings for a new experiment, not replacements for the retained BSM experiments.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds a sensitivity analysis asking whether normalized score error grows with data dimension, using a dimension sweep and fitted trend. v1's empirical studies instead examined BSM's score accuracy and mixture-density recovery; those analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix F explicitly reports five runs per dimension and averaging across runs for the new study. v1 provides no comparable repeated-run reporting for its experiments. No confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests accompany the new averages.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds nearly flat normalized-error results across dimensions 10–200, with a fitted log-log slope of -0.02. The original Gaussian error curves and Gaussian-mixture density plots are identical in v1 Figure 1 and v2 Figure 3, so their relocation supplies no new performance improvement.

T1.justification: The norm-conversion bound in v1 Lemma 7 becomes v2 Lemmas 6/39, with its remainder changed from CL²dΔ^(1/3) log(Nm/δ) to CL²dΔ^(2/3) log(Nm/δ), consistent with the existing derivation. Section 3 also replaces the explicit Rademacher-complexity bound in Equation (6) with an ε²/σ_t² bound and removes the displayed relaxed-error definition. The principal theorems and most appendix proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The v2 abstract explicitly qualifies the nearly dimension-free claim as excluding dependence through log(|H|), a qualification absent from the v1 abstract. The central contributions—joint score-learning bounds, martingale analysis, and BSM—remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 expands the explanation of fine time discretization by separating statistical approximation from stochastic optimization, and adds applicability discussion concerning infinite hypothesis classes and time-varying smoothness. It interprets the new scaling experiment as consistent with the bounds and more explicitly describes BSM evidence as preliminary, leaving empirical performance guarantees open.

D1.justification: New Appendix F documents covariance generation, network inputs and size, learning rate, batch size, training duration, and error normalization. v2 also discloses use of a single Google Colab CPU for the experiments and clarifies the malformed BSM warmup notation as k0 = 250.

R1.justification: v2 adds FYWC24 and VW19 and removes BM02. It expands positioning against worst-case nonparametric diffusion bounds, while deleting the detailed Section 5 comparison with Target Score Matching (DBHWD24), whose citation remains elsewhere.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes broad rewriting and rebalancing: the introduction is streamlined, Section 3 substantially expands explanatory remarks, Section 4 introduces compact notation and clearer proof pointers, and Section 5 is considerably condensed. The hypercontractivity lemma remains in the appendix instead of being repeated in the main text, and the BSM empirical presentation moves to Appendix G.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel dimension-scaling Figure 1 and the proof-dependency diagram in Figure 2. The original BSM Figure 1 is relocated unchanged to Appendix G as Figure 3. Several equations and the contribution list are compacted, while the overall document format remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the dimension-free claim more precise, adds a documented empirical check of dimension scaling, sharpens a lemma's remainder, and improves navigation through the proof. These are useful but limited gains. The added evidence remains synthetic, and compression removes some useful prior-work and BSM explanation, so the revision does not constitute a substantial overall improvement.
